comment: Another price bump for an app that still has no New Episodes folder and plays episodes backwards. Playlists keep me here, but the podcast side is already on Pocket Casts for me, so this just makes me annoyed that I'm paying more for it.

Great, another dollar a month and the artists still get pennies. Free users generate almost nothing for the royalty pool, so raising prices doesn't fix the payout math. I'll keep buying music directly where I can.

Paying more for Premium and still no true lossless, while Tidal already does HiFi for less. I've said this for months. Spotify keeps charging for a feature set that doesn't justify it, so I'm moving to Tidal.

A dollar more doesn't bother me much. Moving years of playlists somewhere else would be a bigger pain than paying a few extra bucks, so I'm keeping my subscription. Still hoping they fix the playlist basics.

The household plan is still worth its weight in gold for my parents, but a price rise when the features we get depend on region is frustrating. We pay the same as everyone else and still get locked out of lossless and AI playlists. Not a good look.

Family goes up to 21.99 and Apple Music is still cheaper with better audio. I'm stuck with Spotify for the playlists and the friend sharing, but every increase makes it harder to justify. Apple Music is getting more tempting.

Doesn't change anything for me. I listen on Bluetooth and I can't hear a difference past 320 anyway, so the price bump is just a number. Plenty of people will complain about it but it's not my problem.
Duo going up $2 is a bit annoying, but when a feature actually shows up it's usually worth the wait. We're staying put for Discover Weekly and whatever comes next. Shrug.

Another price increase and Spotify still plays the same songs in my recommendations. I already pay for YouTube Premium, which includes a music player, so this is basically the nudge I needed. Jam is the only reason I still open it.

Family going from 19.99 to 21.99 is still cheap per person, so I get why we're staying. But no lossless on the family plan and the address stuff is still a mess. Raising the price while the rules are this annoying is rough.
same issue here. Price goes up and the bug I've had since forever is still not fixed. I'm paying for something that doesn't work, and YouTube Music is looking real tempting right now.
Family plan goes up and the artist discography is still missing. Hope they fix it, but it's still a PITA to find albums. Would be easier to be back on YouTube Music.
Paying more for Premium while ads still get jammed into my podcasts? Delete my account. Premium should mean no ads, period. I'm done paying a stupid amount for this.

Price going up in February, and I'm already anxious about getting charged after cancelling. Please make sure the billing period actually ends when it's supposed to. I'll keep the plan for the music but I'm watching my statements.

Been a Premium member for over a decade and I love Spotify for my library and liked songs. A price bump doesn't change that for me. I still wish the recommendations were better, but I'm not going back to Apple Music.
Doesn't affect me, I'm on the free tier. But $13 for Premium is still too much when you can grab YouTube Premium or a cheap country plan. Just pay for premium if you want the good stuff.
12.99 is still cheaper than buying the albums, and I can skip, download and upload my own music. It's pricey but it's worth it for me. Still wish the ads on Premium podcasts would go away.
Premium keeps going up and I'm still on free with playlists that play random songs. Why would I pay more for this? Is anyone else seeing the same thing?

Even at $12.99 it's a bargain: nearly all the music ever made, downloads for flights, and it pays artists. I've been through two increases and it's still the best deal I spend money on. People need to stop complaining about paying for music.
Price going up on a service where shuffle is still broken and smart shuffle keeps inserting junk. I'm on free now and honestly it shuffles better than Premium did. Not paying more for that.
Not paying it anyway. $12.99 for ad-free on a free app that already has locked features is ridiculous at this point. I'll stay on free and use YouTube for full albums.

Going up another dollar for an app that keeps removing features and hiding things. Crossfade is the only reason I'm still here, and Spicetify is doing more for me than the official app. Absolute garbage pricing for what it is.
Student going from 5.99 to 6.99 is a big jump for me. I need the Hulu bundle and the four-year discount is already a worry. Hopefully the verification doesn't break at checkout again.

Price keeps going up and the app still won't play the next song half the time. Support keeps giving the same steps. I already cancelled once and went to Amazon Music, and this price bump just confirms it.
Raising prices while AI slop crowds out real artists in Discover Weekly. They barely pay artists anyway. I already left once and I'm not paying more for fake artists. Pay the artists or leave.

Glad I already cancelled over the AI songs, because this price hike would have been a second reason. Apple Music has been fine and I don't miss the Discover Weekly junk. Spotify still has the playlists I want, but not at this price.

Price goes up and the perks on my tablet are still gone and the mix feature keeps closing. Lossless sounds great when it works, but this update sucks. If the bugs keep going I'm moving to Apple Music.

Family plan is still cheap per person, and $12.99 is still worth every penny for the music, podcasts and audiobooks in one app. The increase is annoying but I'm not switching over it. Just pay for it.
